questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No card is a parcel. All cards are envelopes. Some envelopes are bags. Conclusions: I. All envelopes can never be parcels. II. No card is a bag. III. At least some bags are postcards.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
No card is a parcel.
All cards are envelopes.
Some envelopes are bags.

Conclusions:
I. All envelopes can never be parcels.
II. No card is a bag.
III. At least some bags are postcards.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. All envelopes can never be parcels → Follow (As no card is a parcel and all cards are envelopes. As whole card comes in envelopes and cannot be parcel, therefore it is true.)

II. No card is a bag → Does not follow (As no card is a parcel, all cards are envelopes and some envelopes are bags. As no direct relation is given between card and bags, therefore it is possible but not definite.)

III. At least some bags are postcards → Does not follow (As no relation with postcards is given, therefore it is false).

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.

Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some tears are drops. Some drops are streams. All streams are rivers. Conclusions: I. All tears can never be rivers. II. Some drops are rivers. III. All tears being streams is a possibility.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
Some tears are drops.
Some drops are streams.
All streams are rivers.

Conclusions:
I. All tears can never be rivers.
II. Some drops are rivers.
III. All tears being streams is a possibility.

options.text: Both I and II conclusion follow
options.html: Both I and II conclusion follow

options.text: Both II and III conclusion follow
options.html: Both II and III conclusion follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. All tears can never be rivers → Does not follow (As some tears are drops, some drops are streams and all streams are rivers. As no direct relation is given between tears and rivers, therefore it is false.)

II. Some drops are rivers → Follow (As some drops are streams and all streams are rivers. As whole streams comes in rivers and has some part common with drops, therefore it is true.)

III. All tears being streams is a possibility → Follow (As some tears are drops, some drops are streams. As no statements restricts tears from being streams, therefore it is possible.)

∴ Here, Both II and III conclusion follow.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'A + B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A - B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A $ B' means 'A is the son of B', 'A % B' means 'A is the sister of B', 'A / B' means 'A is the wife of B' and 'A = B' means 'A is the brother of B'. Which of the following means A is the daughter of K? i. A + K / J - P = D ii. J % P = K + A = D iii. K + A / P - D % J iv. D + K = A / P – J
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
'A + B' means 'A is the mother of B',
'A - B' means 'A is the father of B',
'A $ B' means 'A is the son of B',
'A % B' means 'A is the sister of B',
'A / B' means 'A is the wife of B' and
'A = B' means 'A is the brother of B'.

Which of the following means A is the daughter of K?
i. A + K / J - P = D
ii. J % P = K + A = D
iii. K + A / P - D % J
iv. D + K = A / P – J
questions.solution:
iii. K + A / P - D % J → K is mother of A who is the wife of P who is the father of D who is the sister of J.

Here, A is the daughter of K.

questions.question: Which of the following awards was won by Lata Mangeshkar in the year 2001?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following awards was won by Lata Mangeshkar in the year 2001?
questions.solution: Lata Mangeshkar, a legendary playback singer known as the "Nightingale of India," was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001 for her exceptional contribution to Indian music and arts. The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, given for exceptional service of the highest order in any field of human endeavor. Lata Mangeshkar's illustrious career includes receiving other prestigious awards such as the Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award in 1993, the Padma Vibhushan in 1999, and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1989.

questions.question: Which article has a similar provision to that of Article 32 and deals with writ jurisdiction?
questions.questionHtml: Which article has a similar provision to that of Article 32 and deals with writ jurisdiction?
questions.solution: Article 226 of the Indian Constitution empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of both fundamental and other legal rights, providing a broader scope compared to Article 32, which is limited to fundamental rights. Article 32 allows individuals to directly approach the Supreme Court for constitutional remedies in case of fundamental rights violations. Writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari are crucial judicial tools for safeguarding rights and enforcing public duties. High Courts, with their wider writ jurisdiction under Article 226, play a significant role in upholding legal and fundamental rights.

questions.question: Who among the following formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929?
questions.solution: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, a prominent peasant leader, founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in 1929 to address peasant issues in Bihar. The BPKS played a crucial role in mobilizing peasants against the zamindari system and for tenant farmers' rights. Saraswati later became the president of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS), furthering his influence in the peasant movement. The AIKS, formed in 1936, aimed to abolish the zamindari system and improve agrarian conditions nationwide. Saraswati's efforts led to significant agrarian reforms, making him a key figure in the peasant movement in India.

questions.question: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867?
questions.questionHtml: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867?
questions.solution: Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867 to promote religious and social reform in Maharashtra. The Samaj, inspired by the Brahmo Samaj, aimed to promote monotheism, oppose the caste system and eliminate superstitions. It also focused on advancing women's education, widow remarriage, and opposing child marriage. Prominent members included Mahadev Govind Ranade, R.G. Bhandarkar, and N.G. Chandavarkar. The Prarthana Samaj and other social reform movements in India played a crucial role in addressing social issues and modernizing Indian society, laying the groundwork for India's independence and democratic evolution.

questions.question: Who among the following has authored the play 'Nil Darpan'?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following has authored the play 'Nil Darpan'?
questions.solution: Dinabandhu Mitra, a notable 19th-century Bengali dramatist, authored the play 'Nil Darpan' in 1860-61. This play depicts the suffering of indigo farmers under British rule in Bengal and significantly contributed to the Indigo Revolt of 1859-60. 'Nil Darpan' is a pivotal work in Bengali literature and was translated into English by Reverend James Long, who faced imprisonment and fines for its anti-British sentiments. The Indigo Rebellion highlighted the exploitation by British planters and led to reforms. Bengali literature, rich with various genres, includes notable figures like Rabindranath Tagore and Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct order of basicity?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a correct order of basicity?
questions.solution: The basicity of alkali metal hydroxides increases as we move down the group in the periodic table. This trend is due to the increase in the ionic nature and size of the cation, which enhances the availability of hydroxide ions (OH-) to react with acids. Among the given hydroxides, CsOH is the most basic because cesium is at the bottom of the alkali metal group, while LiOH is the least basic because lithium is at the top. These hydroxides are strong bases and highly soluble in water, with their basicity being determined by their ability to dissociate and release OH- ions in solution.

questions.question: Mahendravarman I was the ruler of which of the following dynasties?
questions.questionHtml: Mahendravarman I was the ruler of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution: Mahendravarman I was a ruler of the Pallava dynasty in South India, reigning from 600–630 CE. He was known for his patronage of the arts and architecture, including the construction of rock-cut temples. The Pallava dynasty, which existed from 275 CE to 897 CE, ruled regions of present-day Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka, and significantly contributed to Indian art and architecture.

questions.question: In which city was the first golf club of India situated?
questions.questionHtml: In which city was the first golf club of India situated?
questions.solution: The Royal Calcutta Golf Club, established in 1829 in Kolkata, is the first and oldest golf club in India, and the oldest outside the British Isles. It was founded to serve the British community during colonial times and has a rich history, hosting numerous prestigious tournaments. Golf in India, introduced during the British colonial period, has gained popularity with notable golfers like Jeev Milkha Singh and Anirban Lahiri. The Indian Golf Union oversees the sport's development in the country. The Royal Calcutta Golf Club is located in Tollygunge, known for its challenging course and comprehensive member facilities.

questions.question: What challenge does foreign investment often face in India?
questions.questionHtml: What challenge does foreign investment often face in India?
questions.solution: Foreign investment in India often faces challenges due to an inconsistent regulatory environment. Frequent changes in policies, complex tax laws, and bureaucratic red tape create uncertainty, complicating long-term investment planning. The lack of a unified regulatory framework across different states further complicates the landscape, with foreign investors needing to comply with diverse and sometimes conflicting regulations at both central and state levels.

questions.question: Mohan Veena player, Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the __________ Award in the year 1994.
questions.questionHtml: Mohan Veena player, Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the __________ Award in the year 1994.
questions.solution: Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt is an acclaimed Indian classical musician known for playing the Mohan Veena, a modified slide guitar. He gained global recognition by winning the Grammy Award in 1994 for his album "A Meeting by the River" in collaboration with Ry Cooder. The Grammy Awards, established in 1959 by the Recording Academy, honor outstanding achievements in the music industry. Bhatt's Grammy win highlighted Indian classical music on the world stage. He has also received other prestigious awards like the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan from the Government of India.

questions.question: Lathmar Holi is primarily celebrated in the state of:
questions.questionHtml: Lathmar Holi is primarily celebrated in the state of:
questions.solution: Lathmar Holi, a traditional festival in Barsana and Nandgaon, Uttar Pradesh, involves women playfully beating men with sticks, commemorating the legend of Radha and Krishna. Celebrated a few days before Holi, it attracts many tourists. Holi, the 'Festival of Colors', marks the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil, with celebrations including bonfires, colors, and sweets. Radha and Krishna's divine love story is central to Hindu mythology, inspiring various cultural works. The Braj region, associated with Krishna's early life, is a significant cultural and religious destination in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: When the analysis of population density is done by calculating it through net cultivated area, then the measure is termed as:
questions.questionHtml: When the analysis of population density is done by calculating it through net cultivated area, then the measure is termed as:
questions.solution: Physiological density measures the number of people per unit area of arable land, highlighting the population pressure on productive land. It provides insights into the land's carrying capacity and potential challenges in food production and resource management. This measure is more meaningful than simple population density as it focuses on land that can support human life. In contrast, agricultural density measures the number of farmers per unit area of arable land, indicating agricultural efficiency.

questions.question: Which Indian among the following has his name in Time Magazine's list of '100 most influential people of 2021'?
questions.questionHtml: Which Indian among the following has his name in Time Magazine's list of '100 most influential people of 2021'?
questions.solution: Narendra Modi has been featured in Time Magazine's list of '100 most influential people' multiple times, including in 2021, due to his substantial impact on Indian and global politics. As India's Prime Minister since 2014, he has implemented significant reforms such as Digital India, Make in India, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and Atmanirbhar Bharat. These initiatives aim to enhance India's economic and social landscapes. Modi's leadership during the COVID-19 pandemic, including the vaccination rollout and economic relief measures, also contributed to his recognition. Time Magazine's list honors individuals with profound global influence across various fields.

questions.question: Who is Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology as of July 2023?
questions.questionHtml: Who is Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology as of July 2023?
questions.solution: As of July 2023, Jitendra Singh is the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology. He has been serving in this role following his appointment by the Prime Minister. Jitendra Singh also holds significant roles in the Ministry of Earth Sciences and the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances, and Pensions. His contributions include promoting scientific research and development in India. A Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) oversees a ministry independently, reporting directly to the Prime Minister. The Ministry of Science and Technology aims to advance scientific innovation and research across various sectors.

questions.question: Which plateaus are very fertile because they are rich in black soil that is very good for farming?
questions.questionHtml: Which plateaus are very fertile because they are rich in black soil that is very good for farming?
questions.solution: The Deccan lava plateau is highly fertile due to its black soil, also known as regur soil, which is ideal for farming. This soil retains moisture well, making it beneficial even in dry seasons. Rich in essential nutrients like calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime, it supports diverse agricultural activities. Black soil, formed from volcanic rocks, is particularly suited for growing cotton and is found predominantly in the Deccan plateau, covering parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. Soil fertility is enhanced by its nutrient content and moisture retention capacity.

questions.question: Which of the following states is the biggest producer of Pulses?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following states is the biggest producer of Pulses?
questions.solution: Madhya Pradesh is the largest producer of pulses in India, contributing significantly to the country's total production. The state grows major pulses such as chickpeas, pigeon peas, lentils, and moong beans, supported by favorable climatic conditions and soil types. Pulses, belonging to the legume family, are rich in protein, dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals, and enhance soil fertility by fixing nitrogen. Madhya Pradesh, known as the "Heart of India," also leads in wheat, soybean, and oilseed production. India, being the largest producer and consumer of pulses, relies on them for food security and nutrition, especially for vegetarians.

questions.question: __________ is an industry association and self-regulatory organisation (SRO) whose primary objective is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector.
questions.questionHtml: __________ is an industry association and self-regulatory organisation (SRO) whose primary objective is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector.
questions.solution: The Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) is an industry association representing India's microfinance sector. Recognized as a self-regulatory organization (SRO) by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), MFIN's main goal is to ensure the robust development of the microfinance industry. It promotes responsible lending practices, client protection, policy advocacy, capacity building, and knowledge sharing among members. Additionally, the solution distinguishes MFIN from Self-help Group Associations, which focus on savings and credit among small voluntary groups, and NABARD, which supports rural development but is not specifically dedicated to microfinance.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example?
questions.solution: Cellular Grade Organisation involves functionally differentiated cells that do not form tissues, as seen in Sycon (a sponge). In the Protoplasmic Grade Organisation, all life functions occur within a single cell, exemplified by Paramecium (a protozoan). Cell-Tissue Grade Organisation occurs when cells form tissues, as seen in jellyfish (a coelenterate). Tissue-Organ Grade Organisation involves tissues grouped into organs with specific functions, like in Euplectella, a glass sponge.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?

options.text: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium
options.html: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium

questions.solution: Monoecious plants possess both male (androecium) and female (gynoecium) reproductive organs within the same plant, enabling self-pollination or cross-pollination. Examples include maize, cucumbers, and squash. This differentiates them from dioecious plants, which have male and female organs on separate plants, such as holly and willow. The androecium consists of stamens with anthers that produce pollen, while the gynoecium includes carpels with ovaries containing ovules that become seeds after fertilization. Pollination, essential for fertilization, can be facilitated by wind, water, insects, birds, or animals.

questions.question: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.solution: Project Tiger was launched in India on 1st April 1973 to protect Bengal tigers from extinction and ensure their viable population in natural habitats. The project, administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), initially covered nine reserves and now includes over 50 reserves. The NTCA, a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, was established under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, of 1972. This Act aims to protect wild animals, birds, and plants and create protected areas. Bengal tigers, endangered and native to the Indian subcontinent, have seen population growth due to effective conservation strategies.

questions.question: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.solution: The decomposition of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) into calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) is not a redox reaction because the oxidation states of the elements remain unchanged. A decomposition reaction involves breaking down a compound into simpler substances, often requiring energy input such as heat. Redox reactions involve the transfer of electrons, with one substance being oxidized (losing electrons) and another being reduced (gaining electrons). For instance, the decomposition of sodium hydride (NaH) into sodium (Na) and hydrogen gas (H₂) is a redox reaction, showing changes in oxidation states.

Established in December 1928, BCCI is affiliated with the International Cricket Council (ICC) and is the wealthiest cricket board globally. It manages the Indian cricket team, organizes domestic and international matches, and runs the Indian Premier League (IPL). The Wankhede Stadium is an iconic venue in Mumbai, known for hosting significant cricket events, including the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup final. The ICC, based in Dubai, oversees international cricket and ensures standardized regulations.

questions.solution:
Let sides of the first triangle be a, b, and c.

Let sides of the second triangle be p, q, and r.

Given: a = p, b = q, and a + b + c = p + q + r

Substitute a and b:

a + b + c = a + b + r

⇒ c = r

Thus, all three sides are equal., ∴ Triangles are congruent by SSS.

questions.questionHtml:
The following table shows the total candidates appeared and number of candidates present, in different exam centres – P, Q and R.
Study the table and answer the question that follows.

"Total' denotes total candidates applied for the centre, 'Present' denotes the candidates appeared.
In which year was the number of absentees the second highest in total of all centres?
questions.solution:
Given:

Data on candidates for centres P, Q, and R across years 2016 to 2020, with total and present candidates provided.

Formula used:

Absentees = Total - Present

Calculation:

For each year, calculate total absentees for all centres and identify the second highest.

2016:

⇒ P = 45 - 42 = 3

⇒ Q = 56 - 45 = 11

⇒ R = 55 - 50 = 5

Total Absentees = 3 + 11 + 5 = 19

2017:

⇒ P = 50 - 45 = 5

⇒ Q = 75 - 55 = 20

⇒ R = 45 - 40 = 5

Total Absentees = 5 + 20 + 5 = 30

2018:

⇒ P = 64 - 60 = 4

⇒ Q = 65 - 45 = 20

⇒ R = 65 - 55 = 10

Total Absentees = 4 + 20 + 10 = 34

2019:

⇒ P = 80 - 69 = 11

⇒ Q = 84 - 72 = 12

⇒ R = 70 - 62 = 8

Total Absentees = 11 + 12 + 8 = 31

2020:

⇒ P = 55 - 44 = 11

⇒ Q = 80 - 66 = 14

⇒ R = 90 - 85 = 5

Total Absentees = 11 + 14 + 5 = 30

The absentee totals by year are: 19 (2016), 30 (2017), 34 (2018), 31 (2019), 30 (2020).

∴ The second highest absentee total is 31 in 2019.

questions.solution:
Time taken by Q to fill the cistern = 110 min

Time taken by P to fill the cistern = 110 / 21 min

Rate of Q = 1 / 110

Rate of P = 21 / 110

Combined rate = (1 / 110) + (21 / 110) = 22 / 110 = 1 / 5

Time taken = 1 / (1 / 5) = 5 min

questions.question: R pays ₹100 to P with ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins. The total number of coins used for paying are 40. What is the number of coins of denomination ₹5 in the payment?
questions.questionHtml: R pays ₹100 to P with ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins. The total number of coins used for paying are 40. What is the number of coins of denomination ₹5 in the payment?
questions.solution:
From x + y + z = 40: z = 40 - x - y

Substitute z in 5x + 2y + z = 100: 5x + 2y + 40 - x - y = 100 ⇒  4x + y = 60

For x = 13: y = 60 - 4 × 13 = 8, z = 40 - 13 - 8 = 19

Check: 5 × 13 + 2 × 8 + 1 × 19 = 65 + 16 + 19 = 100

The number of ₹5 coins in the payment is 13.

questions.questionHtml: Mohan borrows a sum of ₹4,22,092 at the rate of 20% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹21,679 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Mohan clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.solution:
Principal = ₹4,22,092, Interest Rate = 20% p.a.

Repayment after 1st year = ₹21,679

Interest for 1st year = ₹4,22,092 × 20/100 = ₹84,418.40

Principal remaining = ₹4,22,092 - ₹21,679 = ₹4,00,413

Interest for 2nd year = ₹4,00,413 × 20/100 = ₹80,082.60

Total amount at end of 2nd year = ₹4,00,413 + ₹84,418.40 + ₹80,082.60 = ₹5,64,914

questions.solution: The correct answer is: Domnica composes lovely tunes. The given sentence is in the Passive voice of the Present Indefinite tense (Object + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject). To convert it into the Active voice, we follow the structure: Subject + V1(s/es) + Object. Here, 'Domnica' becomes the subject, 'composes' is the V1(s) form, and 'lovely tunes' is the object.
